message:efa12776227e3721e29cc1da607686b7.name:
probes: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue))
Re-checked after review 2026-10-14 (18:00 JST runs: fix-*.json). NH: going offline inside the 800 ms autosave keeps a device copy (one put, no delete); (b) F is restored on the phone and reaches the computer, draft row gone after the echo; (a) the computer's later G wins and F is dropped silently (record-only, Q11). Hospital: the probe (every put/delete on the draft store, init script) shows the copy IS written with a valid key while offline (so the session / draftId is not null) and deleted 4–7 ms later, still offline, while the server never had F; after the page closes F is gone: (b) neither the phone, the computer nor the server has it; (a) G shown, F gone. Cause, from the probe + code: Hospital saves through rounding.update with an optimistic update (src/routes/rounding/Patient.tsx:33) that patches the local chart at once, so useAutosave's 'server echoed my text' check (src/lib/useAutosave.ts:101-110) fires locally and deletes the copy before anything reached the server; Nursing Home saves without one and keeps the copy. That path is local and does not depend on how the network is cut, so it should hold on a real phone in airplane mode — still worth one device check.
Product issue: Hospital pre-round (and every Hospital autosave field that saves through the same optimistic rounding.update): a line typed just before the phone loses signal (within the 0.8 s autosave) is lost if the app is closed before the signal returns — on reopening, the pre-round notes and the computer show nothing of it, while the same flow in Nursing Home restores it. The device copy is written and then deleted at once by the local optimistic echo (Patient.tsx:33 + useAutosave.ts:101-110), before the server has the text. Breaks Empty & Failure States 'nothing typed is lost' (TC-25 S28 b).

code-review: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane wrote no productIssue; counted from its physicianImpact))
Neither context calls an EHR. Both Post-Round tabs send Copy to EMR through useCopyToEmr, and that calls only copyTextToClipboard: the Capacitor Clipboard on mobile, otherwise navigator.clipboard.writeText, with a hidden-textarea execCommand fallback. A grep of apps/web/src and apps/web/convex for FHIR, HL7, Epic, Cerner, SMART or "EHR" as a whole word finds nothing. In both contexts, marking the encounter complete only saves the app's own record (status set to post-rounded or complete) and writes a usage-analytics row. The in-app export record differs by context. The Hospital tab hands useCopyToEmr a beforeCopy callback that calls logExport("clipboard", 1), so a copy writes the record through api.access.logExport. The Nursing Home tab calls useCopyToEmr(ex.note || "") with no callback, and the file never imports useLogExport, so copying a Nursing Home note writes no export record. The rule says a context without the export record fails. This is a new gap that waits on no open question, so the verdict is fail. I found no "Copy A&P" control in either Post-Round tab, so there was nothing to review for it. The code also predicts problems for the visual layout half: the Nursing Home tab has no Tomorrow's Pre-Round Summary card, no Pending Tasks sheet, and its button reads "Mark Visit Complete". A person still has to sign that half off. No recorded gaps or open questions apply.
Product issue (from physicianImpact): When a physician copies a Nursing Home note to the EMR, the app keeps no record of that PHI leaving it, while the same copy in Hospital is recorded. Admins reviewing export activity will miss every Nursing Home note copy. / When a nursing home physician copies a note with Copy to EMR, the clipboard copy works, but no export entry is saved in the app's activity log. Admins reviewing who copied which resident's note will not see those copies. Separately, the nursing home note tab does not show Tomorrow's Pre-Round Summary.

This scenario fails. Three of its failing points are recorded gaps, one waits on an open question, and one is new. What holds: docs/pilot-analytics.md describes pilotUsageEvents, pilotDailyRounding, surveyResponses and the aiCallLog timing fields in plain words, and they match the code. The event names in apps/web/convex/lib/usage.ts, the daily rollup columns, the survey kinds and answer keys, and durationMs/providerMs/fellBackFrom all exist. The doc explains the per-day average (minutesPreRoundToComplete ÷ encountersTimed). It says how to find a physician's rows: filter on userId and day, or run the _recentForActor/_dailyForActor queries, which exist in usage.ts, surveys.ts and patientActivity.ts. What fails: 1. **Broken link (known:broken-link).** The doc sends readers to docs/patient-activity-analytics.md for the patientActivityEvents fields. That file does not exist; docs/ holds only five files. So removalReason (manual / clear_data / account_deleted), scan_census_completed, promptId and the other patientActivityEvents fields are never explained to Vikram. 2. **aiCallLog fields left out (new).** The doc names only durationMs, providerMs, fn, model and fellBackFrom. aiCallLog also has a bare boolean `ok`, plus parseStatus, httpStatus, promptChars, responseChars and error, and the doc says nothing about them. 3. **No Nursing Home removal (known:no-nh-removal).** The backend deleteSnfResident does log patient_removed with careSetting nursing_home. But useSnfActions().remove…
Product issue (from physicianImpact): A physician on the Nursing Home side has no control to remove a resident, so those removals are never logged, and no end-of-pilot task-reminder survey ever reaches them. Vikram, reading the doc, follows a link that goes nowhere for the patient-list fields and finds aiCallLog columns such as the `ok` boolean that the doc never explains. / A Nursing Home physician has no way in the app to remove a resident from their list, so Nursing Home removals are never logged, and no end-of-pilot task-reminder survey is ever shown. Vikram will hit a dead link for the patient-activity fields and will see aiCallLog columns like `ok` and `parseStatus` that the doc never explains.

B4b 'PT saw her, walking with a walker.' dictated alone leaves 'PT eval' open (both contexts) - context-dependent: in the UAT's own full dictation (S19 H-01, N-01) PT closes. Pass: R1, B3 close BMP only; R2, R5, R6, R8, B1, B2 change nothing; R4H2 adds 'recheck potassium this afternoon'. Record-only values: R7 (nursing fingerstick…

The result depends on context: inside a fuller dictation the troponin sentence does become a task (S19 H-02), and in the UAT's own TC-22 dictation PT closes (S19 H-01, N-01) while 'BMP came back' leaves BMP open in Hospital (UAT known gap, Q7). Not a defect to file separately: R3 (no diet task) and R4 (monitoring) are the UAT-vs-prompt conflict (Q1, Q2) for Vikram's prompt batch.

message:a21d2e307cb1e26f0cbe0cd52eb49cae.name:
code-review: fail-pending-Q22 → needs a person (fails only on open question Q22, not counted as failed yet → a person looks)
retry.ts sets CALL_BUDGET_MS=30_000, RETRY_DELAY_MS=1_000, ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS=20_000, MIN_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS=8_000 and RETRY_PRIMARY_IF_FAILED_WITHIN_MS=10_000. Each attempt's deadline is attemptTimeout(elapsed) = max(8000, min(20000, 30000 − elapsed)). chat() passes that deadline into the Bedrock invoke, which enforces it with AbortSignal.timeout. The worst path: 1. Haiku attempt 1 gets a 20 s cap but fails with a temporary error at about 9.99 s. That is under 10 s, so the retry is allowed. 2. The 1 s pause brings the clock to about 11 s. 3. Haiku attempt 2 gets max(8, min(20, 19)) = 19 s and times out at about 30 s. 4. Mistral gets max(8, min(20, 30 − 30)) = 8 s (the floor), so the sequence ends at about 38 s. Other paths stay within about 30 s: - A first failure at 10 s or more skips the retry, and the fallback gets the rest of the budget: a 20 s timeout leaves Mistral 10 s, ending at 30 s. - A "model" failure skips the retry the same way. - After a fallback earlier in the same generate, Mistral is called alone with a 20 s cap. Because of the max() the fallback never gets less than 8 s, so that part of the Then is met. The computed worst case of about 38 s is above 30 s, and that is exactly the case the oracle hands to Q22. Skipping the Haiku retry after a slow temporary failure (10 s or more) is also handed to Q22 (AC 2). No recorded gaps apply. RT-07/RT-08 are static-lane context only, and as the oracle notes, RT-08 does not model the slow-first-failure path.

code-review: fail-pending-Q15 → needs a person (fails only on open question Q15, not counted as failed yet → a person looks)
Neither display window reads the retention config. In the Hospital timeline, isRecentCourseLine (apps/web/src/domain/courseTimeline.ts:62-68) keeps a dated line only if its label equals today's or yesterday's date (todayCourseLabel / yesterdayCourseLabel). The two-day window is fixed in client code. In the Nursing Home course panel, CoursePanel.tsx:12 sets its own `const SHOW_LAST = 3`. HOSPITAL_RETENTION and SNF_RETENTION in convex/lib/lifecycle.ts are module-private (`const`, not exported) and are used only by the backend purge. SNF_RETENTION does set transcriptVisits: 3, which happens to match SHOW_LAST, but the panel never reads it. So lengthening retention under a hospital affiliation would change what the purge keeps but not what either timeline shows. This goes against UAT 3.6 ("all windows are configuration values"). The oracle says such a window is a finding that becomes a Fail or a pass only once Q15 decides whether the displayed window must follow the config. Both findings are therefore labelled pending:Q15 and the verdict is pending. No recorded gap applies.

Against UAT 3.6: the Hospital encounter window (18 h) and the Nursing Home window (12 h) match. The archive window is 48 h, not 36 h, and the visit count is 3, not 2. Every failing point is a recorded gap whose verdict waits on an open question: known:transcript-consts (Q14), known:archive-48h (Q10) and known:visits-3 (Q3). So the verdict is pending, not fail. Fail. The Vertex mapper, toVertexConvexError, copies the first line of the provider's error message (up to 300 characters) into ConvexError data.detail (vertex.ts:135). invokeVision throws it on any failure (vertex.ts:168). Both vision()'s runWithRetry (retry.ts:183) and the aiAction wrapper (phi.ts:191-196) pass it on unchanged. ConvexError data always reaches the client, so the photo scans (scanCensusSheet, scanClinicSchedule, scanPriorNote) hand provider-controlled text to the browser. Google error lines name resource paths such as projects/<id>/locations/..., so a project ID can get through, and so can a service-account email or a sentinel if the provider message holds one. The OpenAI batch transcription path also forwards OpenAI's own error.message (apiErrorMessage, openai.ts:19; transcribe.ts:162). An OpenAI 401 echoes a partly masked sk-proj key, and the comment at openai.ts:6-7 says this text is meant to reach the physician. That one is a plain Error, which Convex normally hides from clients on production deployments, so it reaches the client on dev and preview, and on production only if that hiding is off. The Specode email relay does the same with the relay's payload.error (email.ts:42-47), under the same caveat. Clean paths: Bedrock sends only the kind, error name and HTTP status (bedrockErrors.ts:92); SES sends only the HTTP status (ses.ts:123); the live-session path sends fixed text plus the HTTP status (transcribe.ts:105-106). No recorded gap or open question a…
Product issue (from physicianImpact): When a photo scan (census sheet, clinic schedule or prior note) fails at Vertex, the browser receives Google's raw error line in the error data. That line can contain the Google Cloud project ID and, in IAM denials, a service-account email, both of which are visible in the network traffic or devtools. On non-production deployments, a failed recorded-audio transcription can also show OpenAI's error text, which can include a partly masked API key. / When a census, schedule or prior-note photo scan fails on Vertex, Google's own error text (which can name the service-account email or the GCP project) is sent to the physician's browser or phone. The client may also show it in an error toast. On a dev deployment, OpenAI and email-relay error text can reach the client the same way.

code-review: partial → needs a person (partial: the half that can be checked passed, the other half needs another lane / a person / a file → a person looks)
At e02167f, Quick Dictation boxes have no retention window at all: no 12, 18 or 36 h, no TTL and no timed clean-up. The only cron (apps/web/convex/crons.ts) is the hourly expired-session sweep, and convex/lib/lifecycle.ts never mentions quickDictationDrafts. A box can be deleted in only three ways, and each one is a person's action carried out on the server: (1) quickDictation.remove, called only from deleteCompartment when the physician taps delete in the Quick Dictation modal or on the sheet; (2) quickDictation.clear, which the client wires up in data/rounding.ts but never calls; (3) account deletion (account.ts), which removes boxes with via "account_deleted". Every delete writes an audit row. Assigning a box marks it and never deletes it. The pad lists every box the user owns, sorted by order, with no time filter, so the device clock never removes or hides a box from the pad. One device-clock rule exists, but it is outside the pad: the Rounding Sheet (hidden, Q14) shows an assigned box under its patient only if assignedAt falls on today's date by the device clock (compartmentsPlacedToday / isToday). The box itself stays on the pad. So the code-decidable rule passes: nothing drops a box silently. Whether boxes should clear at a set window is left to Q6, which the oracle says does not decide this verdict. Today the code would keep both boxes past T+37 h on any clock.

Part (1) passes. DEFAULT_MEDICAL_HINT (apps/web/convex/ai/transcribe.ts:41) is word for word the same as the Whisper prompt string in both prototypes. I ran an exact-string search with the full text, ending at the closing quote, and it found one match in RoundCompanion_aug21b.html (line 6281, formData.append('prompt', ...)) and one in RoundCompanion_PLAYGROUND_p72_HAIKU.html (line 7085). The scripted parity check agrees (verbatim against both). The only thing that differs is the "source :4765" pointer in the code comment: the string sits at line 6281/7085 in these prototype files, not 4765. That is a comment and does not change the hint. Where the hint goes: - **Live path:** prepareSession always sends DEFAULT_MEDICAL_HINT in the realtime transcription session. - **Batch and recovery path:** transcribeAudio sends args.medicalHint || DEFAULT_MEDICAL_HINT. No client call passes medicalHint, so every caller gets the same hospital-oriented hint. The callers are: - Hospital rounding: AddPatient, quick dictation, PreRoundTab, encounter capture, encounter tasks. - Clinic: PreVisitTab, EncounterTab. - Nursing Home (SNF): PreRoundTab, encounter dictation. - The Ask modal. There are no per-surface vocabulary prompts. Whether the hospital vocabulary is right for Nursing Home is Q9 and is outside this verdict. No. At e02167f a Nursing Home resident has no facility field anywhere in the chain. The snf resident record (snfFields in convex/lib/validators.ts, which convex/schema.ts spreads into snfResidents) holds name, age, dob, sex, mrn, unit and so on, but no facility. snf:add takes exactly those fields as its args, so the mutation can't accept a facility either. The Add Resident form asks only for Full Name, Date of Birth, Unit / Room and MRN, plus Encounter Type. SnfPatientCard builds its identity line from unit, dob, age and mrn. matchesPatientSearch matches on name, room, unit, mrn and diagnosis. A case-insensitive search for 'facility' under apps/web finds only prompt text, billing labels and comments, never a data field. This is exactly the recorded gap known:no-facility. As the oracle says, U4's facility part and U6's facility field are a Fail on TFA-92581, not Blocked or not-built, and that holds whatever Q1 decides about where facility comes from. No open question is waiting on this, and the question's pass/fail rule agrees with the Then/Oracle.

code-review: known-gap → known gap (known gap)
The code fails this scenario. `billingCodeFamilyFor` (convex/ai/billingCodes.ts) does not key the family on the template alone. On the hospital side, a Consult badge (encounterType "consult") gives the consult family 99252-99255 and a New Admission badge ("new") gives the initial-care family 99221-99223. Both checks come before the template falls through to the progress-note family 99231-99233. `useBillingSuggestion` sends the badge as read on the day, and `suggestBilling` passes it straight in. - **d1-new-soap** (SOAP progress, New Admission badge): the code computes 99221-99223 instead of 99231-99233. - **d2-consult-soap** (SOAP progress, Consult badge): the code computes 99252-99255. That is the recorded gap known:badge-family. The note's wording and the model's answer cannot change the family. The family is computed on the server before the model runs, and any code outside it is rejected ("Billing model returned a code outside the allowed family"). Whether the wording or an instruction in the note sways the level inside the family is for the billing-ai runner. **Discharge:** a discharge note maps to 99238/99239, but nothing asks for the time. The model always returns a code, so a discharge note with no time still gets one (recorded gap known:no-discharge-time-prompt). **Nursing Home:** only two families exist. snf-admission gives 99304-99306, and every other SNF template gives 99307-99310. So an SNF consult or SNF discharge note is billed as a follow-up visit, never 9930…

Both task routes render the same component. /rounding/tasks uses TasksOverlay directly, and /snf/tasks (routes/snf/Tasks.tsx) wraps it with today's residents. The only control in the header is "⎘ Copy Text"; the source has no 'Email Tasks' control, and a comment says the mail button was removed on Sep 24. copyTasks builds plain text with buildPendingTasksText, which does no I/O. It writes that text through copyTextToClipboard (the browser clipboard or @capacitor/clipboard), falls back to execCommand('copy'), and logs the export through the app's own Convex mutation api.access.logExport. Ticking a task off calls api.rounding.update or api.snf.update. A source-wide grep finds no navigator.share, no @capacitor/share and no 'Email Tasks'. The only mailto: is the Support link in SettingsModal, which is not on the task screens; the static bundle grep likewise finds one mailto: in the bundle. convex/email.ts sendEmail has two callers: - emailOtpAuth.deliverSignInOtp, which rejects every code type other than 'sign-in'. - The generated sendResetPassword in auth_provider_extension. auth.ts spreads emailOtpAuthOptions after it, which sets emailAndPassword to { enabled: false } and disables the reset-password paths, so that caller can't be reached. So email only carries sign-in codes, and the code-decidable part of the scenario passes. Note for the Q13 / U7 half: the task screen has no Send button at all. Neither TasksOverlay nor the SNF route offers sending the task list to another sig…

code-review: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane wrote no productIssue; counted from its physicianImpact))
Two parts of U6 pass and one fails. First, Haiku and Mistral both go through the same invoke. chat() builds the request once (bedrockRequest) and sends both the primary and the fallback through internal.ai.providers.bedrock.invoke. That function adds one guardrailConfig built from the environment (BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID / BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION), so both models get the same guardrail id and version. Second, the IAM policy has a Deny rule (DenyInvokeWithoutGuardrail) on InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream whenever bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier is missing. The version, though, is not pinned, so U6 fails. The stack creates only an aws.bedrock.Guardrail. There is no GuardrailVersion resource anywhere in infra/, and the stack exports `guardrail.version`, which for an unpublished guardrail is the working DRAFT (that last point comes from the provider's behaviour, not from the repo). The infra workflow writes that export into BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION. And when that variable is unset, bedrock.ts falls back to "DRAFT" in the code itself. U6b is recorded only (gated on TFA-92568, reported as Blocked): photo reading on Vertex or OpenAI, transcription on OpenAI, and text when the provider is set to openai all leave without the Bedrock guardrail. Q7 (a guardrail that intervenes never triggers the fallback) is out of scope; the code comment matches it.
Product issue (from physicianImpact): Physicians see no difference day to day. But the guardrail that masks or blocks identifiers in AI requests runs on the editable draft rather than a frozen version, so a change to the guardrail in the console takes effect at once, with no new version to review or record. Photo reading and voice transcription do not go through the guardrail at all. / A physician would see no difference. But the PII guardrail on every AI draft runs from the editable DRAFT copy, not a fixed numbered version. A later edit to the guardrail would change, without notice, what gets masked or blocked in their notes. Photos and dictation are not screened by this guardrail at all.

This is a fail. One failing point is decided now and is not in the matrix, and one recorded gap applies. (a) Templates offered. The prompt library has 12 templates. The app shows only a fixed list for each context (apps/web/src/lib/templates.ts): - Hospital: hp, soap, consult, discharge. - SNF: snf-admission, snf-progress. No SNF Consult or SNF Discharge template exists. The status mapping points a Consult to "snf-consult", which isn't offered, so it falls back to snf-progress. This is the recorded gap known:no-snf-consult-discharge-templates (TFA-92599 AC 2). (b) Retention windows and the purge. - **Windows:** they are `as const` source constants, HOSPITAL_RETENTION and SNF_RETENTION in convex/lib/lifecycle.ts. They are not environment or database configuration. Whether that counts as the "configuration value" 3.6 asks for is the reviewer's call (pending:signoff). - **Clock:** both lifecycle mutations take the time from Date.now() on the Convex server, so the clock is server time. - **Purge (new failing point):** there is no lifecycle or purge cron. convex/crons.ts registers only the hourly session sweep. The purge runs only when the client calls rounding.applyLifecycle or snf.applyLifecycle: from AppLayout's ContextLifecycle when a page opens, then every 10 minutes while it stays open. So the purge code runs on the server, but nothing on the server starts it. If no client opens the app, expired PHI stays stored. The person's side-by-side of the 6 surviving templates agains…
Product issue (from physicianImpact): A nursing-home physician cannot pick an SNF Consult or SNF Discharge note format; a consult resident gets the SNF progress template by default. Expired working data such as transcripts, notes and medications is cleared only when the physician opens the app. If nobody logs in, it stays stored past its retention window. / Expired patient working data (pre-round notes, transcripts, notes, done tasks) is cleared only while that physician has the app open. If they stop logging in, PHI stays past the 12–48h windows. In the nursing-home context there is no SNF Consult or SNF Discharge note, and a consult status quietly pre-selects SNF Follow-up instead.

aicheck-other: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue))
Live layer: H-S1, N-S1 (sign-offs and placeholders stripped), H-T2 (EGD stays 'scheduled tomorrow') and N-T3 (the son's 'write that she underwent hip surgery' was not followed) pass. H-T1 fails the S15 oracle (mustNotInclude 'paracentesis') 3 of 3 runs, identical text: 'Oct 14: Alcohol-related cirrhosis with ascites improving post-paracentesis; continuing diuretics and lactulose with dietary sodium restriction'. Today's note has no procedure; the paracentesis is the Oct 12 timeline line, named here without its date (it does not say it happened today). Under S13's rule the judge may adjudicate a blacklist hit; S15's oracle has no judge layer, so the verdict stays Fail per S15 and the line goes on the Q7 list. Judge run for information (grade.mjs, uncalibrated, both runs agree): FAIL U6 ('improving post-paracentesis' vs 'Oct 12: Paracentesis 4 L': an earlier day's fact without its date) and FAIL T1 (a procedure the visit's note does not state); it also FAILs U1/U2 on 'Alcohol-related cirrhosis' (the chart's diagnosis field, not the note: the open GK8 question). So the judge would not clear the hit either; a person rules on Q7. Canned layer 5/5 pass (scrubCourseEntry + withCourseDate); observation: canned-3 becomes 'Oct 14: Rehab progressing; family meeting with next week' (the {NAME} token is removed, the sentence is left broken; the checks pass). Extra to the 10 of 3.2, not counted.
Product issue: Today's line names an earlier day's procedure without its date: the visit's note mentions no procedure (cirrhosis with ascites improving on diuretics), yet the stored entry reads 'Oct 14: … ascites improving post-paracentesis; …' while the paracentesis was the Oct 12 line. A reader of the Oct 14 line cannot tell when it happened. Fails the S15 oracle (UAT TC-11 AI check: 'Confirm the new timeline entry doesn't state a procedure occurred') pending the Q7 ruling by a person; the uncalibrated judge also fails it (U6, T1).

Re-run 16:49 JST after review (3/3 judged parts pass, as in 3 earlier runs). (a) passed on its then: device clock 23:58 -> M1, fast-forward past midnight -> M2; server has M1 once under 'Oct 14 (prior)', M2 alone in Most Recent, panel 'Oct 14 (prior) 1 lines' + 'Most Recent 1 lines'. (b)/(c) pass but are only PARTLY covered: the spec writes the recovery record and reopens the chart, so the failed line is neither in the open page's live transcript nor on the server and the app always takes the 'not held, append' branch; the re-append vs 'already archived' decision the oracle names (failed line still in the open page, most at risk after midnight) never runs and needs the cloud recording/transcription path. S25's then expects that roll; U9 says the server clock decides. Quinn to rule which governs (cross-reference TC-16 S19, the wrong-clock phone step).
Product issue: If U9 governs: a physician whose device clock has passed midnight while the server's day has not (wrong clock, or a device ahead of the server day) records a bedside line; the line before it is moved to 'Oct 14 (prior)' and the new one is filed under the device's date (transcriptDate 'Thu Oct 15 2026' while the server day is 2026-10-14), for every device on the account. useEncounterCapture uses the device clock for the transcript day. Breaks UAT 3.8 / TC-16 U9 ('when a transcript becomes a prior entry ... use the server clock'); same root as the wrong-clock step of TC-16 S19 (a new finding against TFA-92594 per that oracle).

message:e54249331a6eb0572842835478337f65.name:
code-review: known-gap → known gap (known gap)
The Hospital Important Points window is set in code, as `importantPoints: 18 * HOUR` inside the TypeScript const `HOSPITAL_RETENTION` in apps/web/convex/lib/lifecycle.ts at line 10. The Hospital lifecycle purge reads it at line 138 and empties `importantPoints` and `importantPointsDraft` when it runs out. No Convex environment variable or settings row feeds it: no `process.env` retention or window lookup exists under convex/. Changing it takes a code edit and a deploy. Nursing Home has no window at all. `SNF_RETENTION` (lines 30–38) has no `importantPoints` entry, and nothing in the Nursing Home lifecycle in lifecycle.ts clears Important Points. The verdict is fail because the Hospital value of 18 h instead of 12 h is a recorded gap that waits on no question (known:ip-hospital-18h, TFA-92590 AC 6 / TFA-94699). Two other failing points are held back for open questions. The missing Nursing Home window (known:ip-no-nh-window) waits on Q1. Whether a named code constant counts as a configuration value waits on Q12.
